Renderer probe

This document exists so the manual build can prove that two renders of the same input give the same bytes. It names no real product and quotes no real document.Footnotes are floated into the page footnote area, which is the feature the realistic manual variant relies on.

The reading order continues in the tabulated values and ends with the two-column section.

Why the probe runs long

The probe has to be long enough for a table to break across a page boundary and for the page counter to reach a value the cross references can resolve to. A shorter probe would pass without exercising either.

Two-column body

Multi-column flow is the last feature this probe covers. The text is filler, but it has to be long enough for the second column to fill, otherwise the column balancing code never runs.

A screw compressor package alternates between a loaded state, in which the intake valve is open and the unit delivers air, and an unloaded state, in which it keeps turning against a closed intake. The controller decides between the two from the header pressure.

A desiccant dryer alternates between its two towers on a timer. While one tower dries the air, the other is regenerated with a small purge flow taken from the dried air.

Every number on this page is invented for the probe and carries no engineering meaning beyond making the layout realistic.
